messages:
inc_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated SRV lookup error rate detected in us-east-2a. Metric: srv_lookup_5xx_rate = 12% (baseline 0.6%). Paging on-call (policy: region-owners).

ashwin_oncall: acked, joining. Investigating now. Can someone drop recent coredns logs and any recent infra changes for us-east-2?

maya_sre_lead: I'm on standby. If this is peering/routing related we'll want network to look immediately. Also please tag any customer-impacting symptoms.

network_ops: fyi we pushed an AZ peering config change at ~1765430700 for us-east-2a->2b (MTU and routes). Change was supposed to be non-disruptive. Rolling back not yet started.

jordan_prod: seeing service discovery timeouts in prod region us-east-2a for internal-services/* when clients do SRV lookups. Errors show up as DNS SERVFAIL and some NXDOMAIN flaps.

ashwin_oncall: grabbing coredns pod logs from one affected node:
```text
[1765432050] coredns: plugin/forward: read udp 10.0.1.12:48212->10.1.10.2:53: i/o timeout
[1765432061] lookup _svc._tcp.internal.svc.cluster.local: read udp: connection timed out
[1765432083] plugin/errors: 2 SERVFAIL
```
Noting repeated timeouts to consul/etcd endpoints? Any consul leader flaps?

rebecca_eng: consul cluster in us-east-2 shows leader unchanged, raft healthy, no large leader elections. But we do see elevated TCP retransmits between nodes in AZ A -> AZ B.

network_ops: pulling routing tables now. Quick check: AS path for peered subnet 10.1.0.0/16 in us-east-2a is showing intermittent blackholed routes for packets > 1400 bytes (MTU mismatch). That could cause DNS/UDP fragmentation issues.

maya_sre_lead: OK mitigation step 1: reduce MTU on coredns host interfaces in us-east-2a to 1400 to avoid fragmentation and get immediate stability. Step 2: if that doesn't help, rollback the peering change. Ashwin, coordinate. Jordan, watch endpoints.

ashwin_oncall: running command on node pool (one node first):
```bash
kubectl exec -n kube-system coredns-0 -- sh -c "ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400"
```
Applying to canary pod in us-east-2a.

ashwin_oncall: canary shows drop in srv_lookup_5xx_rate from 12% -> 1.5% after MTU change. Rolling to remaining coredns pods in the AZ.

liam_cust_success: customer telemetry: about ~3% of external end-user requests to region us-east-2 experienced increased latency/timeouts for 11 minutes. We have ~6 paying customers pinned to that AZ; none have reported escalations yet but SLO alerts triggered. Notifying top-3 accounts as FYI.

maya_sre_lead: good. Keep customers informed, but don't escalate to all customers yet. Network, please prepare rollback plan and change window if MTU fix doesn't fully resolve.

network_ops: rollback plan ready. We can revert peering ACLs and route propagation within 5 minutes; will require a brief route churn but targeted to the peered subnets only. Standby to execute on go.

rebecca_eng: after rolling MTU fix across all coredns in us-east-2a: srv_lookup_5xx_rate steady at 0.5% for 10m. Looks good. Still see occasional retransmits but much lower.

ashwin_oncall: keeping monitoring for 30m. I'll also bump coreDNS forwarders to fallback resolvers in the AZ for extra redundancy:
```yaml
# patch to configmap
forward . 10.1.10.2 10.1.10.3 8.8.8.8
```
Applied on canary then roll.

maya_sre_lead: incident severity: SEV3 (partial degradation, customer impact < 5%). Root cause hypothesis: MTU mismatch introduced by peering change causing UDP fragmentation/timeouts for SRV lookups and inter-az TCP retransmits affecting service discovery.

network_ops: confirmed: peering change adjusted PMTU handling inadvertently. We'll open a vendor ticket and schedule a postmortem with network config change approval added.

liam_cust_success: sent templated note to affected customers: "We observed transient service discovery errors in us-east-2a between 1765432000-1765432700; we've applied mitigations and services are stable. We'll follow up with a technical postmortem."

ashwin_oncall: monitoring shows error rate back to baseline across region. No further timeouts in application logs for last 12m.

maya_sre_lead: moving to resolve. Network, please keep rollback ready but hold for now. We'll include config rollback as part of the postmortem actions and require 2-step verification for future peering changes.

network_ops: acknowledged. We'll add automated MTU checks in change pipeline.

rebecca_eng: quick note for postmortem: capture packet captures from affected nodes, timeline of peering change, and coredns metrics. Also include canary MTU change as mitigation steps and reasoning.

ashwin_oncall: final check: customers notified, metrics stable, oncall handing off to night shift in 40m. I'll add a followup slack thread in #postmortems once we have the URL.

liam_cust_success: 👍 will update account notes with the incident reference.

inc_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated. Incident owner: ashwin_oncall. Severity -> SEV3. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled.

maya_sre_lead: thanks everyone. Good ops.

ashwin_oncall: handing off to @night_oncall in 40m. Leaving monitoring and runbook steps in the incident doc.

jordan_prod: closing loop: no more SRV failures observed, marking as resolved from product side.

rebecca_eng: agree. Will collect logs and open the PM.

inc_bot: Incident closed by ashwin_oncall at 1765432920.
